meta.title: Take a website change request from Asana to live
meta.lead: How a change request becomes a live client site without ever breaking the live site. If you remember one thing: never work directly on main — main is the branch that is the live site. A branch is your own private copy of the site, and nothing on it reaches the live site until someone deliberately merges it.

items.d: Takes a website change request from an Asana task all the way to the live client site without ever putting the live site at risk. Every step that needs a command is a Claude prompt, so nobody has to type a command they do not understand.
Content and code changes to HGM's Next.js client sites hosted on Netlify, requested through Asana and made in VS Code with Claude Code.
Building a new site from scratch, hosting or domain (DNS) changes, and anything on a site that is not one of the Next.js client repositories (code stores) in the hgmwebteam GitHub organization.

blocks.t: Four standing rules
blocks.d: True on every job.

items.d: Work on a branch. Nothing on it reaches the live site until someone merges it.
Not in Google Chat, email or Asana, and never commit .env.local (the site's file of keys; see HGM-SOP-WEB-001). Point people at 1Password.

items.t: Approval is routed, not sent to one person
items.d: Who signs off depends on the change (the table at task 6.1), and silence is not a yes.

items.t: Show the preview, not your laptop
items.d: Your localhost copy proves nothing to anyone else. Check your change on the Deploy Preview URL (Netlify's working copy of your pull request) first.

blocks.text: Phase 1 is once per machine, per site. After that, every job starts at Phase 2.

items.d: Install from the VS Code Extensions panel, then sign in.
Desktop app, signed in to the HGM account with access to the client's vault.
Membership of the hgmwebteam organization. Request from a developer in the Web Team Google Chat group.

Netlify already watches these repositories and builds the preview itself when a pull request (the GitHub page where a branch is reviewed and merged) is opened. You never log in to Netlify or run a deploy command.

blocks.t: Recommended default
blocks.text: Use the Claude prompt everywhere. It checks things a typed command does not, and the credit cost of the mechanical steps is negligible. Task 5.1 matters most: its prompt confirms your change is actually on the Deploy Preview URL, which is the mistake people make most often.
Once per machine, per site. After this, every job starts at Phase 2.

blocks.t: Install the four tools
blocks.d: VS Code, Node.js 20 or newer, the Claude Code extension, and the 1Password desktop app. Links are in prerequisites above.
blocks.expect: Claude Code appears in the VS Code Extensions panel, signed in.

blocks.t: Open a new VS Code window
blocks.d: Choose File → New Window.

blocks.t: Open the Explorer, then click Clone Repository
blocks.d: The Explorer icon is at the top of the left sidebar. With no folder open it offers Open Folder and Clone Repository.

body.caption: The Explorer panel with no folder open.

blocks.t: Paste the repository URL and press Return
blocks.d: Then choose a folder to put the site in.

body.text:
https://github.com/hgmwebteam/<site-name>.git

# taberg-falls  ·  flohom  ·  paradise-pointe
# treetop-escapes  ·  stay-saluda  ·  stay-on-30a
# ridge-and-falls  ·  cohost
body.label: Repository URLs

blocks.t: Or pick the site from the list instead of typing
blocks.d: The same prompt lists every repository in the hgmwebteam organization.

body.caption: Start typing the site name to filter the list.

blocks.t: Click Open when VS Code asks
blocks.d: It asks “Would you like to open the repository?” once the clone finishes. Choose Open, not Open in New Window.

body.t: If VS Code asks you to sign in to GitHub
body.text: Do it. It only asks once per machine.

blocks.expect: The site's files appear in the Explorer panel.

blocks.t: Ask Claude to install the packages
blocks.d: Open Claude Code in VS Code and paste the prompt. It downloads the code the site depends on.

body.label: Claude prompt
body.text: Run npm install in this project and tell me if anything fails.

blocks.expect: It finishes in a minute or two. Once per site, not once per job.

blocks.t: Find the site's .env.local entry in 1Password
blocks.d: Search the site name plus env — for example Taberg Falls .env.local. This file holds the site's credentials. Without it the site still runs, but property photos and prices will not load.

blocks.t: Copy the entry, then create .env.local in VS Code
blocks.d: Copy the entry's entire contents. In VS Code create a new file called exactly .env.local in the top folder of the site (the project root), alongside package.json. Paste, and save. Create it in VS Code, not Finder — Finder hides files whose names start with a dot.

body.caption: The entry. Copy all of it, comments included.

blocks.expect: The site runs locally with photos and prices loading.

blocks.t: If it is not in 1Password
blocks.text: Ask AnhTuan, Leshan, Brandon or Kyle — one of them will have it. Then, with as much warmth as you can manage, ask them to put it in 1Password, because that is where it was supposed to live all along. You are not the last person who will need it. Full procedure in HGM-SOP-WEB-001.

blocks.t: Never send a credential
blocks.text: Do not paste credentials into Google Chat, email, or an Asana comment, and do not add .env.local to the code repository. Git is set to ignore that file on purpose — leave it that way.
Doing Phase 1 in one go instead
Tasks 1.2 to 1.7 are the click-by-click route. This prompt does the same thing in one action.

Clone https://github.com/hgmwebteam/[site-name].git into
this folder, open it, and then run npm install. Tell me if
anything fails.
blocks.label: Claude prompt

blocks.text: Begin here for every new job.

blocks.t: Get onto a clean, current branch
blocks.d: Three things happen here: confirm nothing is half-finished, get the latest code, and make a fresh branch to work on. Git is what tracks every change to the code; a commit is one saved set of changes on your branch.

body.text:
I'm starting a new website change request. Please get me set up:

1. Check I'm on main, that my working copy is clean, and that
   it's in sync with origin/main. If there are uncommitted
   changes I don't recognise, STOP and show me what they are.
   Do not discard anything.
2. Pull the latest main.
3. Create a branch for this job called: fix/[short-description]
   Use fix/ for corrections, feat/ for new features.
4. Confirm which branch I'm on now.

Make no other changes.
body.label: Claude prompt

body.t: Stop if you see changes you do not recognise
body.text: Ask a developer before going further. That is someone's unfinished work, or your own from last time, and carrying it into a new job tangles two changes together.

blocks.expect: Claude confirms your working copy has nothing to commit (a “clean tree”) and that you are on your new branch.

blocks.t: Gather the whole request before opening Claude
blocks.d: Collect the Asana task text, the screenshots, the Loom transcript if there is one, and any follow-up messages.

body.text: It cannot see video or hear audio, and it cannot open your Asana. Paste the transcript text instead. Auto-transcripts garble names badly — if a word looks like a client name, say what you think it means so Claude does not guess wrong.

blocks.text: The step people skip, and the one that prevents the most rework.

blocks.t: Ask for a plan — not for code
blocks.d: Paste the whole prompt, with the request pasted into the marked block.

body.text:
I have a website change request. Do NOT write any code yet.

REQUEST:
"""
[paste the whole request here - Asana text, what the
screenshots show, Loom transcript, follow-up messages]
"""

Before you plan anything:

1. Tell me what branch I'm on and whether it's clean and in
   sync with origin/main. If it isn't, stop and say so.

2. Read the actual files. Do not assume file names, component
   names, or where content lives - find them and cite real
   repo-relative paths and line numbers. If you tell me
   something exists, you must have opened it.

3. Tell me everywhere else this same content or data is
   rendered. Our content is usually shared between pages, so
   one change often needs to land in two or three places.
   Name every one you find.

4. If the request is ambiguous in a way that changes what you
   build, ask me now rather than guessing.

Then give me a plan with:

- Every file you'll add, edit or delete, with real paths
- What changes in each, in plain language
- Risks: what could break, what's hard to undo, and what you
  will NOT be able to check on my machine
- Exactly how you'll prove it works before I look
- Anything in the request you think is a bad idea, and why

Keep it short enough to read in two minutes. I'll approve or
correct it before you touch anything.
body.label: Prompt 1 — planning

blocks.expect: A short written plan naming real file paths. No code written yet.

blocks.t: Read the plan properly before approving it
blocks.d: Check four things: does it do what was actually asked; is the file list proportionate (a one-line copy change touching nine files deserves a question); did it find the other places the same content appears; and did it ask you anything at all — zero questions on a vague request usually means it guessed.

body.text: If anything looks off, say so and ask for a revised plan. Rewriting a plan costs seconds. Rewriting the wrong code costs an afternoon.

blocks.t: Carry out the approved plan
blocks.d: Paste the whole prompt.

body.text:
The plan is approved. Implement it now.

Rules:

- Build exactly what we agreed. If you find partway through
  that the plan was wrong, STOP and tell me. Don't improvise
  a different solution.
- Don't expand scope. If you spot something else worth
  fixing, list it at the end - don't fix it.
- Match the existing style of each file you touch: naming,
  formatting, and how heavily it's commented.

Before telling me it's done, verify it YOURSELF:

- Run: npx tsc --noEmit        (must report no errors)
- Run: npm run build           (must succeed)
- Start the site and LOOK at the change in a real browser.
  Confirm what I asked for is visibly there, and that what
  sits next to it still looks right.
- If it touches a form, an API route, or anything that can
  fail, test the failure path too - not just the happy path.

Then report:

- What you changed, file by file
- What you verified, with the ACTUAL output. Not "it works."
- What you could NOT check on my machine, and why, so I know
  what still needs testing on the preview link
- Then commit, with a message explaining WHY the change was
  made, not just what changed

If any check fails, say so plainly. Don't report success with
the failure buried at the bottom.
body.label: Prompt 2 — execution

blocks.expect: A report naming what changed file by file, with actual command output — not “it works”.

blocks.t: Look at it yourself, locally
blocks.d: Start the dev server (your local test copy of the site), open the page you changed, and drag the window narrow to check mobile.

body.text:
Start the dev server and show me the change. Screenshot the
section you edited at desktop width and again at 390px wide
so I can check mobile. Tell me if anything next to it looks
broken. Then give me the local URL so I can click around
myself.
body.label: Claude prompt

body.text:
Cannot see your change? Hard refresh with Cmd + Shift + R before assuming it failed. Browsers cache hard. Still nothing? Ask Claude to restart the dev server, then to tell you which branch you are on, in that order.

Villa photos blank or green? Expected when .env.local is missing or incomplete. Listing photos and prices come from the booking system. Not a bug you caused — do not report it as one.

blocks.expect: Your change is visible at both widths and nothing beside it looks broken.

blocks.text: Phase 5 — Put it on a preview link
A real URL running real data, that is not the live site. You do not need a Netlify account and you do not run a deploy command — Netlify is already watching these repositories.

blocks.t: Push the branch and open a pull request
blocks.d: Uploading your branch to GitHub (a push) does not create a preview on its own. Opening the pull request is what triggers it.

body.text:
1.  Push the branch: in VS Code's Source Control view,
      click  Publish Branch.

2.  Open the repo on github.com. It offers a
      Compare & pull request  button. Click it, then
      Create pull request.

3.  Wait for the Deploy Preview check, then open the URL.

Do NOT merge yet. The pull request stays open until 6.2.
body.label: Point & click

body.text:
The change is finished and committed. Put it on a preview
link for review:

1. Push my current branch to origin and set upstream.
2. Give me the URL to open a pull request for this branch.
   Do not merge it.
3. Once I tell you the pull request is open, find the
   Netlify Deploy Preview URL for it.
4. Then fetch that URL and confirm my change is actually
   present on it, so I don't send the team a link to the
   wrong build.
body.label: Claude prompt

body.t: If you ever use the Netlify CLI directly
body.text: You should not need to. But if you do, never add --prod. netlify deploy --prod publishes straight to the live site and skips every approval below. If you are unsure, do not run it — open a pull request instead.

blocks.expect: A Deploy Preview check appears on the pull request, then a URL of the form deploy-preview-<number>--<site>.netlify.app.

blocks.t: Confirm you are looking at YOUR version
blocks.d: Open the Deploy Preview URL and check the change is really there before showing anyone.

body.t: The most common mistake on this whole list
body.text: People check the live site, see the old version, and report the change as broken — or see something unrelated and report it as fixed. The live site does not contain your work yet. Only the Deploy Preview URL does. Check the address bar every single time.

body.t: Works locally but not on the preview?
body.text: Usually a setting (environment variable) missing in Netlify. Your computer reads .env.local; the preview reads Netlify's own settings. Ask a developer in the Web Team Google Chat group.

blocks.expect: The address bar shows deploy-preview-<number>, not the live domain.

blocks.t: Send the preview link to the right approver
blocks.d: Comment on the Asana task with the Deploy Preview URL, a one-line summary of what changed, and anything you could not verify yourself. Tag the approver from the table below.

rows: Web, design, or anything touching how the site is built
AnhTuan
Layout, components, a new page, styling, anything in the code
An account or marketing task on a client site
Makenna
Client-supplied copy, a listing description, a campaign landing page
Organization-level, or it commits HGM to something
Gillian
Pricing, terms, legal or policy text, anything on HGM's own site

body.t: Route by what the change is, not who asked for it
body.text: A copy tweak an account manager requested is still a client-copy change, and goes to Makenna. When two rows apply, take the lower one: anything that commits HGM goes to Gillian.
You cannot approve your own change. If AnhTuan made the edit, it goes to Gillian. The point of this task is a second pair of eyes, and self-approval is not that.

blocks.expect: An explicit yes. Wait for it — silence is not approval.

blocks.t: Merge the pull request, then clean up
blocks.d: The pull request has been open since 5.1. Open it on github.com and click Merge.

body.text:
The approver said yes. Help me finish:

1. Confirm my branch is still in sync, and that nothing new
   has landed on main that would conflict.
2. Give me the pull request URL for this branch so I can
   merge it on GitHub.

After I tell you the merge is done:

3. Switch me back to main and pull the latest.
4. Fetch the live site and confirm my change is actually
   there now.
body.label: Claude prompt

blocks.expect: Netlify publishes the change to the live site automatically in 2–3 minutes.

blocks.t: Verify live, then close the task
blocks.d: Open the live site in a private / incognito window, confirm the change, then comment on the Asana task that it is live and mark it complete.

body.text: Your normal browser may serve you a cached copy of the old page, and extensions can hide things that work fine for everyone else. Incognito is closer to what a real guest sees. If a form or section is still blank, try a different network too: DNS filters block form and marketing tools, so it can be invisible to you and fine for everyone else.

blocks.expect: The change is visible to a logged-out visitor.

items.d: Some repositories also define npm run lint and npm run typecheck. Ask Claude to run those too where they exist, in addition to the two checks in Prompt 2.
If .env.local is not in 1Password, get it from a developer and then ask them to store it properly. Do not keep a private copy as the only copy.

Not yet saved to git (committed): ask Claude to throw away your uncommitted edits. Committed but not merged: ask Claude to switch you back to main and leave the branch behind. Nothing on a branch can affect the live site.
Save the remaining budget for task 4.1, which cannot be done another way. The prompts in 2.1, 4.2 and 6.2 are mechanical and cost little.

blocks.t: If you are stuck
blocks.text: Ask Claude first, with Prompt 3 below, instead of guessing at a cause. If it is still unclear — changes you do not recognise, a missing credential, a Netlify setting — ask a developer (AnhTuan, Leshan, Brandon or Kyle) in the Web Team Google Chat group. Who approves a change is routed at task 6.1.

Something isn't working. Before you change any code:

WHAT I EXPECTED:
[describe it]

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS:
[describe it, and paste any error text exactly]

WHERE I SAW IT:
[local / preview URL / live site - paste the exact URL]

Please:

1. Confirm which version I'm actually looking at, so we don't
   debug the wrong build.
2. Find the real cause by reading the code and testing it.
   Don't guess. If you have a theory, prove it before acting
   on it.
3. Tell me the cause in plain language before you fix
   anything, and say how confident you are.

If it turns out I'm mistaken about the problem, tell me
directly.
blocks.label: Prompt 3 — debugging

items: The request is fully done — every part of it, not just the easy parts
You looked at it locally, wide window and narrow
It is on a branch, not on main
A Deploy Preview URL exists and you confirmed your change is on it
The right approver has said yes, explicitly
Anything unverifiable is written in the Asana comment
You checked the live site in incognito after merging
blocks.prompt: Check this change against the final checklist below. For each line, say pass or fail and give the evidence: a command output, a URL, or the approver's message. Make no changes.

items: HGM-SOP-WEB-001 — Store, share, and update client .env files in 1Password
HGM-SOP-OPS-001 — Produce and publish an HGM SOP
Commands here are for HGM's Next.js client sites on Netlify. If a step turns out to be wrong or unclear, say so — a runbook nobody corrects stops being true.
